label: prop:relative
title: Relative cost of a cutoff
checked: The linked edition explicitly restricts the support to consecutive positive odd integers. Taken literally on signed integers, with proper factors defined by 1 < p < |w|, the printed condition on the largest input admits a counterexample. For L=2 take the uniform distribution on −3M and −3M+2, with M the product of the m distinct odd menu primes. Each prime has hit probability 1/2. With fallback cost 3, the full scan costs (m+4)/2 and a singleton is optimal at 5/2. Lean constructs menus of arbitrary size. For positive odd inputs a separate finite proof bounds the two-prime hit probability and proves both the optimal independent cutoff and a quantitative transfer to actual scan costs under finite survival brackets.
remaining: Prove the prime-count estimate and combine all finite bounds to derive the stated logarithmic asymptotic ratio on the corrected positive domain.
